<description>
This migrates the headers presync parameters (`commitment_period` and `redownload_buffer_size`) from being precomputed chainparams to being computed at runtime during startup. This has as advantages:
* Less work for maintainers that need to occasionally run the current `contrib/devtools/headerssync-params.py` script.
* Less room for mistakes in that process.
* Automatically adapts based on time (as opposed to needing to predict the lifetime of the software).

To achieve this, the parameter search algorithm is implemented in C++. It is simpler, because it does not attempt to model the fact that the attacker is forced to submit their headers in batches of 2000. The old Python code did that, but actually got it (slightly) wrong by missing the fact that attackers are capable of strategically deciding to stop the attack in the middle of a batch (found by darosior).

Unit tests and fuzz tests are added, and at the end the old Python code is deleted.
</description>

[2026-10-09] rc:4232684141 inline on src/headerssync.cpp by sipa (member) (edited 2026-10-09):
I forgot where, but you commented somewhere about simplifying to remove the need to search for bufsize.

It turns out that no simplification is needed, since we already have a closed-form function that finds the optimal bufsize when relaxed to real numbers (formerly `cont_bufsize`, now renamed to `real_bufsize`). The integer version doesn't need bisection, it can just round `real_bufsize` up to an integer.

This still leaves a bisection search for the periods. That one is harder to get rid of. It's possible to simplify the `attack_rate` formula a bit more so the result can be found using a closed form expression with the [Lambert W](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambert_W_function) function, and evaluating that needs a loop still too. Simplifying it even further so that the solution can be written explicitly using just elementary functions would lose a great deal of accuracy.
